input.question: why people think that being in cold weather or swimming in cold water can make you sick
input.ground_truth: Because it can. Moving from extreme temperatures one to another can weaken your immune system and that makes it easier for you to get sick. So while it won't directly make you sick to be out in the cold, going between temps is what will do it. Unless it's something like hypothermia. That can make you sick just from being out in the cold.

Now, when you go outside and it's really cold, or when you swim in cold water, your body has to work a little harder to stay warm. Sometimes, this makes your body a little less strong at fighting germs, but it doesn't mean the cold itself makes you sick!

What really happens is that when it's cold, people spend more time inside, close together, and germs can spread more easily from one person to another. Or, after being cold, you might touch your nose or mouth without washing your hands, and if there are germs on your hands, they can get into your body and make you sick.

So, being cold doesn't *directly* make you sick, but it can help germs find a way to get to you more easily. That's why some people think being cold or swimming in cold water can make you sick!
